thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a burst of apiserver 503s in eu-west-2 starting ~09:12UTC. GPU node attach times jump from ~8s to 60s.
raj: yup i'm on it. metrics look like egress path flapping to the NAT gateway cluster.
ellie: is etcd healthy? any leader elections?
maria: etcd looks OK, leader steady. controller-manager pods are restarting slowly though, 1-2 restarts in last 10m.
ops-luke: sre-bot alert: [ALERT] apiserver_5xx_ratio > 0.05 (eu-west-2) :eyes:
sre-bot: automated note: incidents/inc-2024-09-eu-west2 created (priority P2). Link: https://incidents.example/reports/inc-2024-09-eu-west2
raj: grabbing logs from apiserver: 
```
I0909 09:12:24.123456 1 wrap.go:42] http2: server: response stream closed
E0909 09:12:24.223456 1 handlers.go:317] unexpected EOF while proxying to backend
```
ellie: any SNAT exhaustion on the NAT? pack backoffs?
maria: checked cloud NAT metrics — ephemeral ports near saturation for the nodepool handling GPU-assigned pods.
ops-luke: that would explain attach delays — control plane requests to provision GPUs need egress to cloud API endpoints. If SNAT stalls, attach requests time out and controller retries.
raj: quick workaround — we can reduce nodepool churn by throttling autoscaler in eu-west-2 and redirect new job scheduling to eu-west-1/3 temporarily. That'll reduce immediate attach pressure.
ellie: agree, but jobs are latency-sensitive. Redirecting increases cross-region latencies and some customers will complain.
infra-oncall: cost note: redirecting to other regions will spike egress and gpu-on-demand costs. We have ~120% utilization in eu-west-1 right now, can take small burst.
maria: proposal: 1) throttle autoscaler minBurst in eu-west-2 for 30m; 2) bump NAT port allocation (if cloud allows) or add transient NAT gateway; 3) alert customers for small degraded attach times. Thoughts?
raj: ordering — attempt NAT port bump first (fast, infra API call). If that doesn't clear within 5m, flip autoscaler throttle and schedule cross-region fallback.
ellie: add a short controller-manager pod spec change? Might reduce restarts: increase livenessProbe failure threshold from 3->8 temporarily to avoid churn during the egress blips. But that's risky.
ops-luke: agree on bumping probe thresholds only if we know restarts are due to transient API timeouts. Can we confirm?
maria: attaching sample controller-manager logs: 
```
E0909 09:13:01.987 controller.go:240] failed to ensure volume: timed out waiting for the condition
I0909 09:13:02.012 controller.go:256] requeuing pod default/gpu-wkr-7c9 for attach retry
```
raj: looks like API timeouts. I'm going to call cloud API to request NAT port pool increase now.
ops-luke: ping cloud console and also open a ticket for ephemeral port increase — include tags for high-traffic nodepool.
infra-oncall: raising request will cost ~0.6% extra egress budget if we provision an extra NAT gateway for a few hours — acceptable.
maria: if NAT bump fails, i'll run a quick k/switch to scale down new spot instance creation in eu-west-2 and add a placement rule to prefer eu-west-1 until we stabilize.
ellie: also recommend we add a short-lived iptables rule to SNAT from host side? (only if cloud controls aren't possible) may be complex.
raj: update: cloud accepted NAT port increase, applying now. monitoring port utilization.
raj: watch: ephemeral_ports_utilization dropped from 98% -> 55% after the change. attach retries are succeeding more often.
maria: nice, i'm seeing attach latencies down to ~10s now. controller-manager restarts stopped.
ops-luke: boolean decision on autoscaler throttle: keep it as-is for now. If we get more pressure later, we'll enact the throttle playbook.
ellie: follow-up action items:
- raj: confirm NAT change persisted and automation (terraform) can repro the change in infra repo.
- infra-oncall: estimate cost for temporary NAT gateway vs port bump and write brief note for finance.
- maria: prepare a customer message if any long-running jobs were impacted.
- ops-luke: draft a postmortem if this degrades further.

maria: one more thing — can we add a short-term control-plane circuit breaker to avoid thundering attach retries? maybe controller-manager backoff config is too aggressive.
raj: yes, controller backoff params are in k8s controller flags --backoff-retries and --backoff-duration. we can increase base backoff to reduce retry spikes. I'll open a PR with conservative changes (backoff-duration x2) to test in staging.
ellie: add monitoring: new alert for ephemeral_ports_utilization > 85% + apiserver_5xx_ratio > 0.03 to trigger earlier.
ops-luke: agreed. make alert annotate impacted nodepools and include suggested remediation steps.
infra-oncall: closing loop: traffic looks stable, no further 5xx spikes in last 12m. leaving incident P2 open for 2h to monitor.
maria: thanks team. if any regression, re-open channel and escalate. :thumbsup:
